name: PashuSachet Unified Clinical Triage Rules
reference_standard: ICAR-NIVEDI / Department of Animal Husbandry Clinical Protocols

red_flag_triggers.label_en: Severe Left Flank Distention / Bloat with Respiratory Distress
red_flag_triggers.label_mr: पोटाचा डावा भाग प्रचंड फुगणे / धाप लागणे
red_flag_triggers.message: EMERGENCY: Immediate veterinary intervention required. Call 1962 toll-free hotline or rush to nearest polyclinic.

red_flag_triggers.label_en: Continuous Convulsions / Inability to Stand or Lift Head
red_flag_triggers.label_mr: सतत झटके येणे / जनावर उठू न शकणे
red_flag_triggers.message: EMERGENCY: Severe neurological or toxic distress. Contact mobile veterinary emergency unit immediately.

red_flag_triggers.label_en: Sudden Profuse Bleeding from Natural Orifices (Nose/Mouth/Anus)
red_flag_triggers.label_mr: नाक, तोंड किंवा गुदद्वारातून अचानक रक्तस्त्राव
red_flag_triggers.message: EMERGENCY SUSPICION (Anthrax): DO NOT open carcass. Call 1962 and isolate area immediately.

safe_first_aid: Isolate the affected cattle in a clean, shaded, fly-screened stall immediately.
Apply pure neem oil or herbal fly repellent around unruptured skin to prevent vector bites.
Provide clean, cool drinking water mixed with oral electrolytes and jaggery.
Clean weeping skin sores with 0.1% potassium permanganate or mild antiseptic solution.
WARNING: Do NOT administer human painkillers (paracetamol/diclofenac) without a prescription.
Keep the animal on clean, dry, soft bedding (straw, sand, or rubber mat).
Gently wash mouth blisters with 1% potassium permanganate or mild alum wash.
Dress foot lesions with antiseptic fly-repellent ointment (e.g. Lorexane / herbal spray).
Do not herd infected animals through village lanes or shared grazing areas.
Strip the affected quarter clean every 2 to 3 hours into a disinfectant cup to relieve udder pressure.
Apply cold water compresses or ice packs to the hot, swollen quarter.
DO NOT CONSUME OR SELL MILK from the affected animal; discard safely.
Ensure veterinary inspection for intramammary infusion and systemic anti-inflammatory therapy.
Move the animal to a dry, well-ventilated, draft-free stall.
Keep the animal warm with jute sack coverings during winter or cold night winds.
Administer eucalyptus steam inhalation if facilities permit.
Seek prompt veterinary antibiotic and bronchodilator treatment.
Withhold concentrated grains and lush green fodder for 12 hours.
Provide clean drinking water with a pinch of common salt and baking soda (sodium bicarbonate 50g in water).
Offer palatable dry fodder (wheat straw/jowar kadbi) in small amounts.
Monitor body temperature; if fever develops or condition persists >24 hours, request vet visit.
CRITICAL EMERGENCY: Isolate immediately; notify veterinary officer without delay.
Keep head elevated to ease severe breathing difficulty.
Do not stress or force the buffalo to walk.
Isolate buffalo on clean, soft bedding.
Gently wash mouth lesions with 1% potassium permanganate.
Apply fly-repellent wound cream to foot clefts.
Isolate infected goats immediately from the rest of the flock.
Provide oral rehydration salts (ORS) in clean water to prevent fatal dehydration.
Keep the goat warm and clean eye/mouth crusts with warm sterile cotton.
Emergency condition: call veterinarian immediately.
Immediately stop all grain/concentrate feed to the flock.
Administer activated charcoal slurry if advised by doctor.
